newsitem.title: UK: Rollercoaster LME copper surges back above $2,400.
newsitem.headline: Rollercoaster LME copper surges back above $2,400.

text.p: Copper and aluminium prices flew higher on Thursday afternoon, shrugging off an early downside correction in a last-minute buying spree.
Light conditions made for whippy trading on the London Metal Exchange (LME), with three-months copper trading in a sweeping $2,355-$2,409 range.
It settled at $2,403 per tonne, up $28 on the day, after fund buying into midday dips triggered buy-stops and sent prices bubbling higher, traders said.
"Copper and aluminium have been well supported by the trade and specs today," said analyst Robin Bhar of Brandeis. "There has been good dip buying -- these metals don't seem to want to go lower."
Technical analysts had been forecasting downside corrections in both aluminium and copper after weeks of steady strong gains.
Aluminium was similarly sold down to a low of $1,655 before snapping higher to finish the kerb with a $16 gain at $1,689.
"The markets were undecided all day so when the buying came in everyone went along with it," a trader said.
Stronger than expected January U.S. factory and durable goods orders may have encouraged funds to jump into the metals, analysts and traders said.
The market was keeping a close eye on Friday's LME stocks report. Traders were uncertain what the report would hold, although only small drawdowns in copper and aluminium would dampen sentiment.
The other metals also basked in the strength of flagship copper.
Zinc also staged a comeback, shooting above the recent $1,240 breakout level.
Tin also moved higher, against predictions that it would test downside support amid weakening technicals. It was last at $5,910, a rise of $75.
Nickel held its own for most of the day, then ticked higher to end $70 stronger at $8,150.
Lead was also firmer at $683, up $7, after initially sliding below the $680 level.
Cash/threes backwardation also flared out again to a $4 bid, after briefly moving into contango midday.
Aluminium alloy was quietly firmer at $1,560, versus $1,553/55.
